chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿImrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl, that he asked Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and he said:

I had performed one circuit for him, then dawn rose. He said: Perform salat (prayer), then return and complete your saʿy. And in the obligatory tawaf, it is not appropriate that one speak in it except with du'a (supplication), dhikr (remembrance) of Allah, and recitation of the Qur'an.

He said: And in the supererogatory one, a man may meet his brother, greet him with salam, and speak to him about something from the affairs of the Hereafter and the world. He said: There is no harm in it.
So the proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation, not obligation and requirement.

key_terms.الدُّعَاءِ: supplication directed to Allah during worship
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory, referring here to non-obligatory tawaf
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, indicating a preferred but non-obligatory ruling
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, marking the time when the prayer becomes due
key_terms.ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ: remembrance of Allah through devotional utterance
key_terms.سَعْيَكَ: your saʿy, the ritual traversal performed in hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.طَوَافُ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf, the required circumambulation
key_terms.قِرَاءَةِ الْقُرْآنِ: recitation of the Qur'an during tawaf

ai.seo_question: Is speaking during obligatory or supererogatory tawaf permitted in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses speech during tawaf, distinguishing between obligatory and supererogatory tawaf. In obligatory tawaf, speech is restricted to du'a, dhikr, and Qur'an recitation, while limited worldly and otherworldly conversation is permitted in supererogatory tawaf. The final statement explains that this restriction is to be understood as recommended rather than strictly obligatory.
